I've seen a few times now where people confuse a poster replying to them for a poster earlier in the thread. I believe that this confusion is related to the way that comment replies are linked from one's inbox: you have the option to go a single comment up via "parent" or straight to the new comment via "permalink," but neither of these options show the full context of the conversation, and thus can easily lead to confusion when one has been having multiple conversations in a short period, as one is wont to do on the internet.

The "context" feature that reddit uses circumvents this confusion rather well, and is actually an incredibly well-programmed feature. Would it be possible to integrate something similar here? We could call it something different if we wanted, like "subthread," and have the feature link to the full series of comments going upwards from the inboxed comment all the way to the highest parent response in the thread. I feel that this would make for better communication and improve the Voat experience quite a bit.

Thoughts/comments?
I definitely like the "subthread" idea. I had often found myself wanting a feature just like that back on reddit. Having it as a one click option would be pretty great.

Right? I feel like doing a full subthread view (not expanding every single comment, just a direct line up to the top-most parent) would be a great way to take a useful feature Reddit has and then make it even better.

Hopefully it wouldn't be too difficult to implement, I tend to open all the parents before replying anyway just to refresh the context for myself and it would be super convenient to do that with a single click.
